newsitem.title: DENMARK: Denmark's Berendsen sees 96 result down.
newsitem.headline: Denmark's Berendsen sees 96 result down.

text.p: Denmark's Sophus Berendsen on Monday forecast 1996 full-year results before tax and associated company earnings of 145 million crowns, down from 1995's 275 million and compared to a first-half 1996 figure of 107 million.

Reporting the expected second half downturn, a company statement noted losses of between 30 and 40 million in its Electronics and Data division and said that divisional chief Niels Hjertholm had resigned.
The latest forecast excludes 37.5 percent-owned Rentokil, the British firm which contributed 533 million crowns pre-tax to Berendsen's first-half group result of 640 million crowns.

The statement said that the Electronics and Data division had in 1996 faced exceptionally hard market conditions neccesitating cost-cutting and the elimination of several product lines. --Steve Weizman, Copenhagen newsroom +45 33969650
